boarding pass printer

Motionby @heydamir2026-09-03inspora pageoriginal post

What it is

A boarding pass 'prints' out of a slot at the top of a phone screen like a thermal printer - ticket feeds down into view, sways gently, then retracts; infinite loop.

Media

Frame-by-frame

0-10%
'Upcoming Trip' screen; dark printer slot near top; only the barcode stub of the pass peeking out.
10-30%
Pass feeds downward: route header, date, passenger, gate/seat rows reveal top-to-bottom like paper from a printer; soft shadow grows under the leading edge.
30-50%
Pass fully printed, hanging from slot: pendulum sway (+-1.5deg) and micro settle bounce; perforated bottom edge + barcode visible.
50-65%
Retract: pass slides back up into the slot; shadow shrinks.
65-85%
Slot nearly empty; brief pause.
85-100%
Next print cycle starts; loop.

Mechanics

trigger
autoplay loop
elements
printer slot bar, pass card inside overflow-hidden window, soft drop shadow
properties
translateY (feed/retract), rotate (pendulum), shadow opacity/scale
timing
feed ~1.6s, hold ~1.2s with sway, retract ~1s, pause 600ms
easing
feed cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1); sway sine 2.5s; retract ease-in
loop
infinite print-hold-retract

Build prompt

Build a thermal-printer boarding-pass loop. Fixed slot bar (dark rounded rectangle with 8px opening) near the top of a mobile trip screen. The pass (white ticket: route header MSQ 20:00 -> ALA 03:10 with plane icon, passenger/date/seat rows, barcode, perforated bottom edge via repeating radial-gradient mask) sits in an overflow:hidden wrapper aligned to the slot. Print: translateY -100% -> 0 over 1.6s cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1) so it feeds out of the slot; grow a blurred shadow under the leading edge (shadow tracks the reveal boundary, opacity 0->0.25). Hold: pendulum rotate(+-1.5deg) origin top center, 2.5s sine, plus a 200ms settle bounce (translateY +4px spring) when the feed completes. Retract: translateY -> -100% over 1s ease-in, shadow fades. Pause 600ms, loop. Add paper grain and 1px perforation ticks on the pass bottom edge.
Source: inspora.design - original interaction by @heydamir. Teardown snapshot Sep 2026.
